posts.body_html:
Looking quite delightful this year! S. leucophylla 'Helmut's Delight' reminds me a lot of S. leucophylla AJ01 for some reason...maybe they're from the same original population? I haven't seen any wild leucos in recent years that quite resemble these genotypes, although the populations they originally came from could possibly still exist. photos taken 9/16/18:




Check out those tall leuco 'puffy cheeks' in the background, that clone is without a doubt a winner because it performs year after year:

posts.body_html: You have a really beautiful and fascinating plant. I do wonder where it was originally taken from by the suppliers of the Australian supermarket you mentioned, and I imagine if Helmut found this in a supermarket then sadly the original wild population is likely extinct, especially as this has unique characteristics. I am very glad he managed to buy and distribute this though as it is an incredibly pretty and also unique-looking leuco. I have one and it is about to open it's first fall pitchers

posts.body_html: I've had it for 5 years and it grows a single pitcher in spring and another in autumn, but not much else seems to happen. It probably just needs feeding. Some clones don't seem to need much to thrive, others get stuck if they don't capture anything.
